entry.text: Rise and shine, kid. Another day, another victory in our heroic struggle against health campaigns and self-control.
And to celebrate the triumph - give me a tin of Morley and papers.

options.text: Someone left me a tooth last shift

response.text: Charming. Even tied up with a bow.

options.text: What was it you asked for?

response.text: God... Alright, let's go slow. See that red-and-white tin on the shelf, says Morley? Yes, that's tobacco. Good.
Now, on the counter, your left hand, the greenish box with papers in it. Open it. Take exactly one pack. That's it.

news.text: соц опрос мне кажется тут надо сделать такой небольшой чекап поинт если что-то непонятно или остались вопросы или хз напомнить что-то..... и вот с челом это можно обсудить

options.text: Should I just offer it to everyone?

response.text: Heh, like you're brave enough for that... From what I gathered, if you can't slip it in quietly, better not. No need to make things weirder.
Talk to people, play some mind games. Drop the jar in with their order if you're sure enough. Just know they might notice later, or not return it at all - then it's gone.

options.text: You know anyone missing a tooth?

response.text: Ha. In Larris? Could be half the town.
But if it hasn't gone dark yet, it's not ancient. Someone probably dropped it fairly recently.

options.text: Got any idea how I could slip it to someone?

response.text: ...Hm. Well. Talk to people, feel them out. If you're sure, slip the jar into their bag. Just know they might spot it later, or not give it back. And then it's gone.

checkout.text: Thanks. Have fun with your cancer sticks and human leftovers.

checkout_notooth.text: Thanks. Oh, and about that small jar by the till... It has a human tooth in it.
Let's say it's... something somebody left, to pass on to someone else... only nobody's, you know, a hundred percent sure who.
Can't say more, but if you feel like playing dental Cinderella, go ahead.

check.text: ...And good work with the till. Did it neater than me. Keep it up, that's yours to handle at the end of every shift now.

check_irresponsible3.text: ...And the till. Thought I asked you to count it last shift. Maybe I forgot, maybe you slacked off — either way, do it today. End of every shift, it's your job.

bye.text: Alright, I'm off to greater things.

entry.text: Good morning, and may your day be as bright as your smile and as lovely as your heart.
Blessed morning, sweet face. We're here for cigarettes, but decided to be a little poetic about it today.
What lulls from a drawer and eases your blues, holds the colour of veins and a yesterday bruise?

click.text: ...What about smoking it behind the pharmacy again? No one ever bothers us there.
Mmh... I was thinking we could go by St. Dymphne's today. Just for a minute, before work.
I feel like I should talk to Father Jean-Noël. About the organ...
Huh? About what? Don't tell me you suddenly feel guilty and want to tell him about... that, do you?
What? No! Oh God, calm down.
It's just... Matron asked something weird yesterday. If Father Jean-Noël had started getting ready for the organ festival, or... something like that.
I said something like, "yeah, haha, with a dead organ", but she just gave me this confused look. Like she had no idea what I meant.

response.text: ...That's impossible. Father Jean-Noël has to report to the bishop every week. And if the bishop knows, you can be sure Matron does too.
Mm. Not this time. Doesn't feel like our kind of day for that.

repeat.text: What lulls from a drawer and eases your blues, holds the colour of veins and a yesterday bruise?

response.text: Ah, darling... It's Lavender Fleuries. Like those violet lavender sachets people keep in drawers to calm their nerves.

options.text: Didn't Yves write that the organ was falling apart?

response.text: Umm. I've seen those reports. They always said the organ was in some kind of... stable condition. I kept wondering if it's really supposed to sound like that, but I thought maybe I just don't understand music, so I never spoke up.
Mhm. Usually nothing dramatic - just how things are going in the parish, what they might need from the diocese. But the organ dying feels like... kind of a big thing to leave out, doesn't it?
Maybe to cover for that troublesome boy he let help out? Father Jean-Noël doesn't exactly have the best reputation with the dioces-
Babette. We should probably get going.
...Right. Sorry.

wrong_price.text: Hmm. That's not what it cost last time.

checkout.text: Thanks. So... I'll stop by Father Jean-Noël on my way.
...Alright. I'll just head straight to the hospital.

entry.text: Good afternoon, {{name_yves}}. I need an ashtray for the workshop.
Accidentally retired the old one, and now customers are flicking ash into empty tobacco tins. Not great.

response.text: Maybe there was something weird there?
(If that doodle wasn't just a joke, and the left panel's hiding something... Yves would've found it by now, right?)
Hm... That side was much worse than the rest of the buffet. Pipes knocked out of place, some mold, bit of rot. But nothing too special. Old things fall apart funny sometimes.
...Strange thing to ask.
(Alright. Let's pull that thread.)
Couldn't it have been prevented? I heard bellows are often the first thing to go. Problematic part.
...Most irritating to check.

...Bellows are a pain, yeah. And in case of this particular organ, what was the point anyway? It wasn't only about bellows, the whole left half was a mess. Pipes knocked out of place, some mold, bit of rot. Keyboard too - half the keys loose, a few straight-up gone.
So... yeah. Whole thing was dying already.
And you helped it die faster?

Helped it die? I did every bloody check they asked for, twice a year, reports all nice and proper, just how the diocese wants them. Told them it was falling apart and needed proper repairs, not patch jobs and prayers. No reaction. Nothing changed.
Eventually I stopped checking it properly. Just looked at the parts you could see without crawling in all the way. Figured if they didn't care, why should I?

options.text: So you cracked first, like a loser?
All that ass and no squat

response.text: Well. Maybe I could've done my job better.
...I'll take it off the repair cost. Not much, but fair's fair.
You can be really nasty, huh?

options.text: So you wrote in your reports that the organ was falling apart?

response.text: Of course I did. Wrote it plain as day, every time. Handed them to Father Jean-Noël like I was supposed to.
...Guess the folks in the city don't care much about this town. Same thing when we asked them to send a stand-in organist while ours was... eh, away for a while. Nothing ever came of it.
Holding on, but it's getting tougher. Even booked extra sessions with the nun.
The one who stick needles in your...
Heavens, no. Still got all my teeth, and I intend to keep them. Just the ears.
(Okay, so the Tooth isn't his.)
That's right.
...What, to grow whiskers? No, no. The ears.
Cruel joke, {{name_yves}}. Didn't crawl back to it. Just an ashtray.

ears.text: If you're curious, talk to Sister ???. She does nerves, hiccups and bad habits.

checkout.text: Thanks. Ashes to ashes, tin to bin. Take care, {{name_yves}}.

entry.text: Evening! I've made a decision. Today, I become mysterious.

response.text: Not during my shift. I refuse to have this on my conscience.
(...I always hated being called her bad influence.)
Oh come on. Taking a moral stance? You?
Ugh. Fine. No pink cigarettes today.
Who am I to stop you.
(...They always called me her bad influence anyway.)
Perfect. Thank you.

options.text: What was behind organ's left panel?

response.text: ...Oh. So you found that.
Okay, look... Before you say anything - I swear I was super careful. But you know how it is... You start examining small weird cracks and suddenly you're halfway inside a giant antique instrument.
I found that weird puzzle in a huge pile of letters and thought it might be some secret message, hidden confession or, I don't know, a cursed artifact or something. It just felt so... important.
Letters to the Seal
A lot of scribbled notes, marbles, dead moth in a matchbox... even a half-full tube of condensed milk. A whole hidden world stuffed behind that panel.
I think the local kids were using it as their secret mailbox. And maybe also a bit of a rubbish bin...
It's kind of adorable. But yeah, no ancient mysteries or secret artifacts.
Well... there is a tiny chance that I knocked something loose. A pipe or... tube? Some old metal thing. It made a really sad dying sound.
I panicked, obviously. But I tried to put everything back how I found it... Ish. I mean, it still played at the next mass, so I convinced myself it was fine.
Also... let's be real, all that junk the kids were cramming in there did more damage anyway. Probably. So, you know, I'm not the only one to blame...

organ.text: I'll... sort something out. Make up for it somehow.
